**Given:** The Axiom of Choice; a nonempty complete metric space $(X,d)$; and closed sets $(F_n)_{n\ge1}$ covering $X$.

[A1] The Axiom of Choice permits the countable recursive choices of nested balls used below ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]).



1.1 Suppose every $F_n$ has empty interior. Choose a nonempty open ball $B_0\subseteq X$. Since $F_1$ is closed with empty interior, $B_0\setminus F_1$ is nonempty and open; choose a closed ball $\overline B(x_1,r_1)\subset B_0\setminus F_1$ with $0<r_1\le2^{-1}$. [given, A1, construct]

2.1 Inductively, if $\overline B(x_n,r_n)$ has been chosen, its interior $B(x_n,r_n)$ is a nonempty open set. The closed set $F_{n+1}$ has empty interior, so $B(x_n,r_n)\setminus F_{n+1}$ is nonempty and open; choose a closed ball $\overline B(x_{n+1},r_{n+1})$ contained there with $0<r_{n+1}\le2^{-n-1}$. Thus the closed balls are nested, and the $n$th ball avoids $F_n$. [step 1.1, A1, construct]

3.1 The nested centers form a Cauchy sequence because for $k\ge n$ one has $x_k\in\overline B(x_n,r_n)$ and $r_n\to0$. Completeness gives a limit $x\in X$; each closed ball contains every later center and hence contains $x$. Therefore $x\notin F_n$ for every $n$, contradicting $X=\bigcup_nF_n$. Thus some $F_n$ has nonempty interior. [given, step 2.1, A1] ∎

**Given:** Full AC; Fréchet spaces $E,F$; and a continuous surjective complex-linear map $T:E\to F$.

[A1] Full AC is the set-choice postulate ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]).

[F1] A Fréchet space is a Hausdorff locally convex topological vector space with a countable seminorm basis and a compatible complete metric ([[def-qftx-gaga-frechet-space]]).

[F2] In a nonempty complete metric space, a countable closed cover has a member with nonempty interior ([[lem-qftx-gaga-baire-category-complete-metric-spaces]]).



1.1 Fix an open neighborhood $U$ of $0$ in $E$. Since $E$ is metrizable and locally convex, choose an absolutely convex neighborhood $W_0$ whose closure is contained in $U$. Choose a decreasing sequence of absolutely convex neighborhoods $W_n$ such that $W_n\subseteq2^{-n}W_0$ and, for each of the first $n$ members $p_1,\ldots,p_n$ of a defining countable seminorm family, $p_j(x)\le2^{-n}$ for all $x\in W_n$. For each fixed $j$, the seminorms of the tails are bounded by a convergent geometric series, so any series $\sum_{n\ge1}x_n$ with $x_n\in W_n$ is Cauchy in the Fréchet topology and converges by completeness. Its partial sums lie in $W_0$ because $W_0$ is convex and balanced and $\sum_{n\ge1}2^{-n}=1$; hence its limit lies in $\overline{W_0}\subset U$. [A1, F1, given, construct]

2.1 For each $n$, the neighborhoods $kW_n$ ($k\ge1$) cover $E$, since every neighborhood of $0$ in a topological vector space is absorbing. Surjectivity gives $F=\bigcup_{k\ge1}kT(W_n)\subseteq\bigcup_{k\ge1}\overline{kT(W_n)}$. By [F2], some $\overline{kT(W_n)}$ has nonempty interior; scaling shows $\overline{T(W_n)}$ has nonempty interior. If $O_n\subseteq\overline{T(W_n)}$ is a nonempty open set, then $O_n-O_n$ is an open neighborhood of $0$ contained in $\overline{T(W_n)-T(W_n)}\subseteq\overline{T(2W_n)}$; scaling by $1/2$ gives a neighborhood $V_n\subseteq\overline{T(W_n)}$. Shrink $V_n$ so its diameter tends to $0$ in a compatible metric on $F$. [A1, F1, F2, step 1.1, algebra]

3.1 Take $y_1\in V_1$. If $y_n\in V_n$, then $y_n\in\overline{T(W_n)}$, so choose $x_n\in W_n$ such that $y_{n+1}:=y_n-Tx_n\in V_{n+1}$. The series $x=\sum_{n\ge1}x_n$ converges in $E$ and belongs to $U$ by step 1.1, while $y_n\to0$ by the diameter choice. Continuity of $T$ gives $Tx=\sum_{n\ge1}Tx_n=y_1$. Hence $V_1\subseteq T(U)$, so $T(U)$ is a neighborhood of $0$. [A1, F1, step 1.1, step 2.1, construct]

4.1 Let $O\subseteq E$ be open and choose any $y\in T(O)$ with $Tx=y$ for some $x\in O$. There is an open neighborhood $N$ of $0$ with $x+N\subseteq O$. Step 3.1 gives a neighborhood $V$ of $0$ contained in $T(N)$, so $y+V\subseteq T(O)$. Every point of $T(O)$ is therefore interior, hence $T(O)$ is open and $T$ is open. [step 3.1, given, algebra] ∎

**Given:** Full AC; Fréchet spaces $E,F$; a continuous linear quasi-epimorphism $g:E\to F$; and a compact continuous linear map $h:E\to F$.

[F1] Full AC is the set-choice postulate ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]).

[F2] A continuous surjective linear map between Fréchet spaces is open ([[lem-qftx-gaga-frechet-open-mapping]]).

[F3] A Fréchet space is a Hausdorff complete metrizable locally convex vector space ([[def-qftx-gaga-frechet-space]]).



1.1 First, if a continuous linear map $T:E_0\to F_0$ between Fréchet spaces has finite-codimensional image, then that image is closed and $T$ is open onto its image. Since $\ker T$ is closed, the quotient $E_0/\ker T$ is Hausdorff and locally convex. Its quotient seminorms from a countable defining seminorm family metrize it. It is complete: choose a decreasing absolutely convex neighborhood basis $U_n$ in $E_0$ with $U_{n+1}\subseteq\tfrac18U_n$; from a Cauchy sequence of cosets choose a subsequence whose successive differences lie in the quotient images of $U_n$, lift those differences to $U_n$, and sum. For each defining seminorm, the lifted series has a geometric tail bound, so completeness of $E_0$ gives a limit and the subsequence, hence the original Cauchy sequence, converges. Thus $E_0/\ker T$ is Fréchet. Choose a finite-dimensional algebraic complement $S$ to $T(E_0)$ in $F_0$. The induced map $(E_0/\ker T)\oplus S\to F_0$, $([x],s)\mapsto T(x)+s$, is a continuous linear bijection between Fréchet spaces. By [F2] it is a homeomorphism. The closed subspace $(E_0/\ker T)\oplus\{0\}$ therefore maps to the closed subspace $T(E_0)$, and the quotient map $E_0\to E_0/\ker T$ shows that $T$ is open onto $T(E_0)$. [F2, F3, given, construct]

2.1 Choose a finite-dimensional complement $S$ to the closed finite-codimensional subspace $g(E)$ and let $q:F\to F/S$ be the quotient. The induced $\bar g=qg:E\to F/S$ is a continuous open surjection: $g:E\to g(E)$ is open by step 1.1, and $q|_{g(E)}:g(E)\to F/S$ is a continuous bijection between Fréchet spaces, hence a homeomorphism by [F2]. The induced $\bar h=qh$ is compact. Choose an absolutely convex neighborhood $U$ of $0$ in $E$ such that $K:=\overline{\bar h(U)}$ is compact, and set $V=\bar g(U)$; then $V$ is an open absolutely convex neighborhood of $0$ in $F/S$. Compactness gives $b_1,\ldots,b_N\in K$ with $K\subseteq\bigcup_j(b_j+\tfrac12V)$. Put $S_0=\operatorname{span}\{b_1,\ldots,b_N\}$ and let $p:F/S\to(F/S)/S_0$ be the quotient. Then $p(K)\subseteq\tfrac12p(V)$. [F2, F3, step 1.1, given, construct]

3.1 Write $G=p\bar g$, $H=p\bar h$, and $W=p(V)$. The map $G$ is surjective and $G(U)=W$. For any $y_0\in W$, choose $x_0\in U$ with $Gx_0=y_0$ and set $y_1=y_0-(G+H)x_0=-Hx_0\in p(K)\subseteq\tfrac12W$. Inductively, if $y_n\in2^{1-n}p(K)\subseteq2^{-n}W$, choose $x_n\in2^{-n}U$ with $Gx_n=y_n$; then $y_{n+1}:=y_n-(G+H)x_n=-Hx_n\in2^{-n}p(K)$. Thus $y_n\in2^{1-n}p(K)$ for all $n\ge1$. [F1, step 2.1, construct, algebra]

4.1 It remains to choose these lifts so their series converges. Let $(U_j)_{j\ge1}$ be a decreasing absolutely convex neighborhood basis in $E$ with $U_{j+1}\subseteq\tfrac18U_j$. For fixed $j$, the increasing open sets $G(2^nU_j\cap\tfrac12U)$, $n\ge1$, cover $G(\tfrac12U)=\tfrac12W$: every point of this image has a lift in $\tfrac12U$, and the sets $2^nU_j$ exhaust $E$. Their images are open because $G$ is open. Since the compact set $p(K)$ lies in $\tfrac12W$, compactness gives an integer $N(j)$ such that $p(K)\subseteq G(2^{N(j)}U_j\cap\tfrac12U)$; enlarge the $N(j)$ if needed so they strictly increase. Keep $x_0$ separate. Retain the finitely many tail lifts $x_n$ for $1\le n\le N(1)$ from step 3.1 and their resulting residual $y_{N(1)+1}$. Thereafter choose each new lift recursively using its current residual, and define the next residual by $y_{n+1}=y_n-(G+H)x_n$; the bounds of step 3.1 continue to hold because each new lift still belongs to $2^{-n}U$. For each block $N(j)<n\le N(j+1)$, since $y_n\in2^{1-n}p(K)$ choose $k_n\in K$ with $p(k_n)=2^{n-1}y_n$. Choose $z_n\in2^{N(j)}U_j\cap\tfrac12U$ with $Gz_n=p(k_n)$, which is possible by the defining inclusion for $N(j)$, and put $x_n=2^{1-n}z_n$. Then $Gx_n=y_n$ and $x_n\in2^{N(j)+1-n}U_j\cap2^{-n}U$. The sum over this block lies in $2U_j$, because the coefficients $2^{N(j)+1-n}$ sum to less than $2$. The sum of all later block bounds is at most $2\sum_{k\ge1}8^{-k}U_j=\tfrac27U_j\subset U_j$, so tails after sufficiently late blocks lie in any prescribed neighborhood in the basis. The same bound applies to partial sums within each block, so arbitrary tails also tend to zero as the block index grows. The tail partial sums are Cauchy in the defining seminorms; by [F3] they converge to $x=\sum_{n\ge1}x_n\in E$, with $x_0$ excluded. [F1, F3, step 3.1, construct]

5.1 The compact set $p(K)$ is bounded in the locally convex space $(F/S)/S_0$: for any balanced neighborhood $Q$ of zero, the dilates $tQ$ ($t>0$) cover the space, so compactness gives a finite subcover of $p(K)$ and, since $Q$ is balanced, one largest dilate contains all of $p(K)$. Therefore $y_n\in2^{1-n}p(K)$ tends to $0$. The recursively maintained residual identity gives $(G+H)\sum_{n=1}^m x_n=y_1-y_{m+1}$. Passing to the limit using continuity yields $(G+H)x=y_1$. Thus $(G+H)(x_0+x)=y_0$, so $G+H$ maps onto $(F/S)/S_0$. It follows that $F=(g+h)(E)+q^{-1}(S_0)$, where $q^{-1}(S_0)$ is finite-dimensional because $S$ and $S_0$ are finite-dimensional. Thus $(g+h)(E)$ has finite codimension; step 1.1 makes it closed, proving that $g+h$ is a quasi-epimorphism. [F3, step 1.1, step 2.1, step 3.1, step 4.1, algebra]

6.1 The conclusion holds for every full-AC Fréchet pair and every pair of maps with the stated hypotheses, including the case $g(E)=F$ (then $S=0$) and the case $h=0$ (then one may take $K=\{0\}$). [F1, step 2.1, step 5.1] ∎

**Given:** Full AC; two cochain complexes of Fréchet spaces with continuous differentials; a continuous cochain map $\rho^\bullet$; a degree $q\ge0$; compactness of $\rho^q$ and surjectivity of the induced cohomology map for the finiteness assertion.

[F1] A Fréchet space is Hausdorff, complete, metrizable and locally convex ([[def-qftx-gaga-frechet-space]]).

[F2] A compact perturbation of a quasi-epimorphism between Fréchet spaces is a quasi-epimorphism ([[lem-qftx-gaga-schwartz-compact-perturbation]]).

[F3] A continuous surjective linear map between Fréchet spaces is open ([[lem-qftx-gaga-frechet-open-mapping]]).

[A1] Full AC is the set-choice postulate used by [F2] and [F3] ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]).



1.1 Write $Z_E^q=\ker(d^q)$, $B_E^q=\operatorname{im}(d^{q-1})$, and likewise $Z_F^q,B_F^q$, using the actual degree $q-1$ term, or the zero space when that term is absent. The cocycle spaces are closed kernels of continuous maps, so they are Fréchet by [F1]. Define continuous linear maps on the Fréchet space $Z_E^q\oplus F^{q-1}$ by $g(x,y)=\rho^q(x)+\delta^{q-1}(y)$ and $h(x,y)=-\rho^q(x)$, with codomain $Z_F^q$. The cochain-map identity ensures both images lie in $Z_F^q$. [F1, given, construct]

2.1 The map $g$ is surjective: for $z\in Z_F^q$, surjectivity of $H^q(\rho^\bullet)$ gives $x\in Z_E^q$ and $y\in F^{q-1}$ with $z-\rho^q(x)=\delta^{q-1}(y)$. It is therefore a quasi-epimorphism by [F3]. The map $h$ is compact because it factors the compact map $\rho^q$ restricted to the closed subspace $Z_E^q$ through the finite product projection. [A1, F1, F3, given, step 1.1]

3.1 Apply [F2] to $g$ and $h$. Their sum is $(g+h)(x,y)=\delta^{q-1}(y)$, whose image is exactly $B_F^q$. Hence $B_F^q$ is closed and finite-codimensional in $Z_F^q$. The quotient $Z_F^q/B_F^q=H^q(F^\bullet)$ is consequently Hausdorff and finite-dimensional. [A1, F2, step 2.1]

3.2 For the openness assertion, let $\sigma^\bullet:E^\bullet\to F^\bullet$ be any continuous cochain map whose induced $q$th cohomology map is surjective, and put $Z_E^q=\ker d^q$, $Z_F^q=\ker\delta^q$. The map $G:Z_E^q\oplus F^{q-1}\to Z_F^q$, $G(x,y)=\sigma^q(x)+\delta^{q-1}(y)$, is surjective by the same representative argument as in step 2.1, hence open by [F3]. If $O$ is an open subset of $H^q(E^\bullet)$, its inverse image $\widetilde O$ under the quotient map $Z_E^q\to H^q(E^\bullet)$ is open and saturated by coboundaries. Then $G(\widetilde O\times F^{q-1})=\pi_F^{-1}(H^q(\sigma^\bullet)(O))$, where $\pi_F:Z_F^q\to H^q(F^\bullet)$ is the quotient map. The left side is open because $G$ is open; by the quotient topology the image $H^q(\sigma^\bullet)(O)$ is open. [A1, F1, F3, given, step 2.1, construct]

4.1 Steps 3.1 and 3.2 prove the two conclusions in the Statement. The argument uses no bound on the complex length and also applies in degree $q=0$; for a complex concentrated in nonnegative degrees, its absent degree $-1$ term is zero. [step 3.1, step 3.2] ∎

**Given:** Full AC; an integer $m\ge1$; and a Hartogs-pseudoconvex domain $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb C^m$.

[A1] Full AC is the set-choice postulate ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]).

[F1] Smooth forms of bidegree $(0,j)$ form sheaves $\mathcal A^{0,j}$ with differential $\bar\partial$ and $\bar\partial^2=0$ ([[def-bigraded-complex-differential-forms]]).

[F2] Under full AC, the local Dolbeault lemma makes the smooth $(0,\bullet)$-complex exact in positive degrees on polydiscs ([[thm-dolbeault-lemma-polydisc]]).

[F3] A $C^1$ function with all coordinate $\bar z$-derivatives zero is holomorphic ([[thm-cauchy-riemann-characterization-in-several-complex-variables]]).

[F4] Each sheaf of smooth differential-form modules is acyclic for global sections on every open subset of a smooth manifold ([[thm-smooth-function-module-sheaves-are-acyclic]]).

[F5] An exact resolution by global-section-acyclic sheaves computes right-derived global sections ([[thm-acyclic-resolution-theorem-for-right-derived-functors]], [[def-sheaf-cohomology-derived-global-sections]]).

[F6] On a Hartogs-pseudoconvex domain in $\mathbb C^m$, every smooth $\bar\partial$-closed $(0,q)$-form is $\bar\partial$-exact for $1\le q\le m$ ([[cor-dolbeault-vanishing-pseudoconvex-domain]]).



1.1 On each coordinate polydisc in $\Omega$, [F2] says the sequence of sheaves $0\to\mathcal O_\Omega\to\mathcal A^{0,0}\xrightarrow{\bar\partial}\mathcal A^{0,1}\xrightarrow{\bar\partial}\cdots$ is exact in positive degree. Its degree-zero kernel is exactly $\mathcal O_\Omega$: a smooth function in that kernel has all $\bar z$-derivatives zero and is holomorphic by [F3]. Thus it is an exact sheaf resolution on $\Omega$. [F1, F2, F3, given]

2.1 Each resolution term is a sheaf of modules over smooth functions and is $\Gamma(\Omega,-)$-acyclic by [F4]. The acyclic-resolution theorem [F5] therefore identifies $H^q(\Omega,\mathcal O_\Omega)$ with the cohomology in degree $q$ of the global smooth Dolbeault complex. [A1, F4, F5, step 1.1]

3.1 For $1\le q\le m$, [F6] makes every closed global smooth $(0,q)$-form exact, so the degree-$q$ cohomology in step 2.1 is zero. For $q>m$, the complex has no $(0,q)$-forms on an $m$-dimensional complex manifold, so its degree-$q$ cohomology is zero as well. Hence $H^q(\Omega,\mathcal O_\Omega)=0$ for every $q>0$. [A1, F1, F6, step 2.1, algebra] ∎

**Given:** Full AC; an $r$-dimensional complex manifold; a coherent analytic module on a neighborhood of $V$; finitely many relatively compact coordinate polydiscs with intersection $V$ nonempty; and an exact length-$2r$ partial free resolution on a neighborhood of one participating polydisc. The resolution is only assumed exact through the penultimate free term.

[A1] Planned local Oka interface: assume AC; on every finite-dimensional complex manifold $M$, $\mathcal O_M$ is coherent, coherent modules are closed under kernels, cokernels and finite extensions, and for every coherent $\mathcal F$, point $x$ and finite $\ell\ge0$ there is a chart neighborhood with an exact partial finite-rank free resolution $\mathcal O^{p_\ell}\to\cdots\to\mathcal O^{p_0}\to\mathcal F\to0$, exact at the module and each free term except the leftmost. No global free resolution is asserted ([[thm-qftx-gaga-analytic-oka-coherence]]). The manifested batch 63 carrier has a ready record that is hash-stale; this use remains conditional.

[F1] A continuous plurisubharmonic exhaustion on a domain can be regularized to a smooth strictly plurisubharmonic exhaustion under AC ([[lem-smooth-regularization-of-psh-exhaustion]]).

[F2] A bounded domain with a smooth plurisubharmonic exhaustion is Hartogs pseudoconvex ([[lem-smooth-psh-exhaustion-implies-hartogs-pseudoconvexity]]).

[F3] A Hartogs-pseudoconvex domain has zero positive-degree derived cohomology for its holomorphic structure sheaf ([[lem-qftx-gaga-scalar-pseudoconvex-acyclicity]], [[cor-dolbeault-vanishing-pseudoconvex-domain]]).

[F4] If $W\subseteq\mathbb R^m$ is open and $\mathcal G$ is any sheaf of abelian groups on $W$, then $H^j(W,\mathcal G)=0$ for $j>m$ ([[lem-qftx-gaga-euclidean-sheaf-cohomological-dimension]]). This is ordinary cohomology, not a compact-support assertion. The current batch 65 item has a full inspected proof and a non-owner ready record, but that record is hash-stale; its metric Čech comparison prerequisite is also hash-stale. This input remains conditional.

[F5] A short exact sequence of sheaves gives the long exact sequence of derived sheaf cohomology ([[thm-long-exact-sequence-sheaf-cohomology]]).

[F6] The coordinate polydisc $D=\{|z_j-a_j|<R_j\}_{j=1}^r$ has the smooth strictly plurisubharmonic exhaustion $\rho_D(z)=-\sum_{j=1}^r\log(R_j^2-|z_j-a_j|^2)$; its Levi matrix is diagonal with entries $R_j^2/(R_j^2-|z_j-a_j|^2)^2>0$. Finite maxima preserve plurisubharmonicity, and holomorphic coordinate changes preserve it ([[def-plurisubharmonic-function]], [[def-levi-form-and-strict-plurisubharmonicity]], [[thm-c-two-levi-criterion-for-plurisubharmonicity]], [[thm-stability-operations-for-plurisubharmonic-functions]], [[thm-holomorphic-pullback-of-plurisubharmonic-functions]]).



1.1 Choose the chart of $D_{i_0}$ and write $V$ in those coordinates. For each $D_i$, the function $\rho_{D_i}$ in [F6] is a smooth plurisubharmonic exhaustion of $D_i$; on $V$ it remains plurisubharmonic after composing with the holomorphic chart transition. The continuous function $\rho:=\max_{1\le i\le s}\rho_{D_i}$ is plurisubharmonic by [F6]. If a sequence in $V$ leaves every compact subset of $V$, it approaches the boundary of at least one of the finitely many $D_i$, and the corresponding $\rho_{D_i}$ tends to $+\infty$. Thus $\rho$ is an exhaustion of $V$. [F6, given, construct]

2.1 Each connected component $V_\alpha$ is a bounded domain in the chart of $D_{i_0}$ and inherits the continuous plurisubharmonic exhaustion $\rho$. Apply [F1] to obtain a smooth plurisubharmonic exhaustion on $V_\alpha$, then [F2] to conclude that $V_\alpha$ is Hartogs pseudoconvex. By [F3], $H^q(V_\alpha,\mathcal O)=0$ for $q>0$, hence $H^q(V_\alpha,\mathcal O^{p})=0$ for every finite rank $p$. [A1, F1, F2, F3, step 1.1]

3.1 Restrict the assumed partial resolution to $V_\alpha$ and define $K_{-1}=\mathcal F|_{V_\alpha}$ and $K_j=\ker(\mathcal O_{V_\alpha}^{p_j}\to\mathcal O_{V_\alpha}^{p_{j-1}})$ for $1\le j\le2r$, with $K_0=\ker(\mathcal O_{V_\alpha}^{p_0}\to K_{-1})$. Exactness of the resolution through the penultimate free term gives short exact sequences $0\to K_j\to\mathcal O_{V_\alpha}^{p_j}\to K_{j-1}\to0$ for $0\le j\le2r$, where at $j=0$ the rightmost term is $K_{-1}$. By [A1] each $K_j$ is coherent, and by step 2.1 the middle free sheaf in each sequence is acyclic in positive degree. [A1, F5, step 2.1, given]

4.1 The long exact sequence [F5] for each short exact sequence in step 3.1 therefore gives, for every $q>0$, isomorphisms $H^q(V_\alpha,K_{j-1})\cong H^{q+1}(V_\alpha,K_j)$ for $j=0,1,\ldots,2r$. Iterating yields $H^q(V_\alpha,\mathcal F)\cong H^{q+2r+1}(V_\alpha,K_{2r})$. The chart identifies $V_\alpha$ with an open subset of $\mathbb C^r\cong\mathbb R^{2r}$, so [F4] makes the last group zero because $q+2r+1>2r$. [F4, F5, step 3.1]

5.1 The components of the open set $V$ are disjoint open subsets and are at most countable because the chart is second countable. Sheaves on their disjoint union are tuples of sheaves on the components; global sections are products, and products of abelian groups are exact under AC. Applying componentwise injective resolutions therefore gives $H^q(V,\mathcal F)=\prod_\alpha H^q(V_\alpha,\mathcal F)=0$ for $q>0$ by step 4.1. [A1, step 4.1, algebra] ∎

**Given:** Full AC; a finite-dimensional complex manifold; a coherent analytic module; and a finite presentation on a chart-open set $V$ whose global section map is surjective.

[F1] Coherence means local finite generation and local finite generation of every finite relation sheaf ([[def-qftx-analytic-coherent-module]]).

[F2] At each point $x$, the local ring $R=\mathcal O_{M,x}$ is Noetherian with maximal ideal $\mathfrak m_x$. For a finite $R$-module $E$, its analytic Krull topology is induced by the finite-dimensional quotients $E/\mathfrak m_x^kE$ with their usual complex-vector-space topologies; it is Hausdorff because $\bigcap_k\mathfrak m_x^kE=0$. For a finite submodule $L\subseteq R^{p_0}$, Artin–Rees makes the topology induced from $R^{p_0}$ agree with the intrinsic Krull topology on $L$, so $L$ is closed ([[thm-holomorphic-germ-ring-is-noetherian]], [[thm-artin-rees-lemma]], [[thm-krull-intersection-theorem]]).

[F3] Cauchy estimates control every finite jet by a uniform bound on a larger compact polydisc, and locally uniform limits of holomorphic functions are holomorphic ([[thm-cauchy-estimates-on-a-polydisc]], [[thm-locally-uniform-limit-of-holomorphic-functions-in-several-variables]]).

[F4] A Fréchet space is a Hausdorff complete metrizable locally convex vector space ([[def-qftx-gaga-frechet-space]]).

[A1] Full AC is the set-choice postulate ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]).

[A2] Planned Oka interface: assume AC; on every finite-dimensional complex manifold $M$, $\mathcal O_M$ is coherent, coherent modules are closed under kernels, cokernels and finite extensions, and every coherent $\mathcal F$, point $x$ and finite integer $\ell\ge0$ have a chart neighborhood with an exact partial finite-rank free resolution $\mathcal O^{p_\ell}\to\cdots\to\mathcal O^{p_0}\to\mathcal F\to0$, exact at the module and every free term except the leftmost. No global free resolution is asserted ([[thm-qftx-gaga-analytic-oka-coherence]]). Its current ready record is hash-stale, so this use is conditional.

[A3] Full exact planned local supplier claim: “Assume AC. Let $F$ be coherent analytic on a neighborhood of a point $x$ in $\mathbb C^N$. There is a coordinate polydisc $W$ about $x$ such that for every nonempty coordinate polydisc $D\subset W$ and every $q>0$, $H^q(D,F|_D)=0$. Scalar sheaf cohomology on such $D$ is computed by its smooth Dolbeault resolution. One can choose $W$ subordinate to a partial finite-rank free resolution of $F$ of length exceeding $2N$. The assertion is local in the supplied resolution neighborhood; no untwisted projective Cartan A/B or global Stein generation theorem is asserted.” ([[thm-qftx-gaga-analytic-local-coherent-polydisc-acyclicity]]). The exact planned item ID is absent from the batch 65 manifest and has no readiness record. The manifested alternate-ID theorem has a matching stronger interface, but its current Step 1 record is escalated because that record identifies hash-stale readiness for its Oka and bounded-degree-relations inputs. Only the positive-degree polydisc vanishing clause is used below, conditionally on the exact planned supplier.

[F5] A short exact sequence of sheaves gives the long exact sequence of derived sheaf cohomology ([[thm-long-exact-sequence-sheaf-cohomology]]).
